newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate pares rise on firm peso.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate pares rise on firm peso.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates checked earlier advances driven by U.S. long bond yields to end up 60 basis points at 23.50 percent when the peso gained strength in late trade, dealers said.
"Overnight rates climbed at the open, but the forex market held steady and that made secondary rates calm down," a trader said.
Overnight Cetes had reached as high as 24 percent in early trade.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts, meanwhile, closed 1.5 centavos firmer at 7.9420/7.9460 per dollar.
Overnight rates on bank paper ended up 40 basis points at 25.40 percent.
U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds were down 20/32 in late trade to yield 7.12 in late trade.
One money market analyst said secondary rates managed to resist trending upwards in line with U.S. yields as Mexican rates were still attractive and drawing foreign demand.

"(Domestic) rates are attractive to foreign investors who have no reason to bail out here. On the contrary, as long as U.S. rates keep rising money will keep flowing in and that will hold the peso steady, even if U.S. long bond yields climb above 7.15 percent," he said.
Banco de Mexico drained 2.333 billion pesos from the markey by auctioning five secondary auctions, which it assigned at rates between 25.23-25.58 percent.
Liquidity of 2.705 billion pesos was scheduled to return to the system from prior central bank participation.
